text: The name states the behaviour: the function generates the even integers between a and b of any size. This conflicts with 'return the even digits between a and b' and with the example generate_integers(10, 14) => [].
a >= 0 and b >= 0 (non-negative); a call with 0 must also follow the rule, so whether 0 counts as an even digit matters.
Return the digits in another form: as digit characters (strings such as '2'), or as another sequence type such as a tuple or a generator.
The even single-digit numbers 2, 4, 6 and 8 only (0 not counted).
The integers strictly between min(a, b) and max(a, b), ends excluded. Contradicts the example generate_integers(2, 8) => [2, 4, 6, 8].
The even single-digit numbers 2, 4, 6 and 8 only (0 not counted).
The integers strictly between min(a, b) and max(a, b), ends excluded. Contradicts the example generate_integers(2, 8) => [2, 4, 6, 8].
Non-decreasing: each element is at most the next, so a value may repeat (matters only if the same digit can be found more than once).
Illustrative only: it conflicts with 'between a and b' read as excluding the ends (which gives [4, 6]), and the statement prevails.
Illustrative only: it conflicts with 'between a and b' read as from a up to b (which gives [] when a > b), and the statement prevails.

Illustrative only: it conflicts with 'even digits' read as even integers (as the name generate_integers suggests, giving [10, 12, 14]) or as the even digits written in 10 to 14 (giving 0, 2 and 4), and the statement prevails.
